document_summary: The recording opens mid-discussion of matching humans with jinn companions. Most of the first half is a detailed presentation of structural Quranic calculations using Sura numbers, verse totals, zeros for Bismillah, sequential verse numbers, 6,346 verses, 12,806 component numbers, 37,088 digits, word totals, and exclusion of Quran 9:128–129. Rashad says he sometimes accepts blame or deliberately makes mistakes to demonstrate his humanity and destroy idolatry. The closing emphasizes the camel, punishment, ancestral following, ego, and independent thought by age forty.

sections.title: Deliberate mistakes, accepting blame, and destroying idols
sections.summary: Rashad says one of his important tasks is destroying idols. He may refuse to defend himself, accept an accusation, change his mind, or even deliberately make a mistake so followers see that he is fallible and do not idolize him.
related_questions: Why did Rashad say he made deliberate mistakes?
How was this supposed to prevent idolatry?
